_meta.purpose: Hand-curated ground-truth anchor points for rarity-pill calibration. Replaces the iNat-circular backtest with externally-sourced visitor encounter probabilities pulled from peer-reviewed studies, NPS operational reports, long-term ecological monitoring outputs, and well-documented field-guide consensus. Each anchor is a (parkId, species, expected probability) triple at a specific season + visit-effort context.
_meta.scoring: scripts/calibrateAgainstAnchors.js loads this file, looks each species up in the static cache, computes the model's predicted probability for the matched (season, effort) context, and reports Ranked Probability Score (Epstein 1969) plus a reliability diagram. RPS is proper and distance-sensitive — predicting `exceptional` when truth is `likely` is penalized more than predicting `unlikely`.

anchorSchema.species: common name as used in the cache (case-sensitive)
anchorSchema.season: spring | summer | fall | winter | year-round (year-round means averaged across all seasons)
anchorSchema.visitorEffort: casual (default) | expert | drive (matches the popup effort selector)
anchorSchema.probability: anchor encounter probability (0-1) — the externally-attested chance of seeing this species on a typical visit in the named context
anchorSchema.tierExpected: guaranteed | very_likely | likely | unlikely | rare | exceptional — derived from probability via RARITY_THRESHOLDS
anchorSchema.confidence: high | medium | low — how directly the source measures per-visit visitor encounter (high = explicit visitor-survey or operational sighting log; medium = trusted field-guide consensus or ecological monitoring; low = inferred from related metrics)
anchorSchema.rationale: 1-2 sentence note on why this anchor is trustworthy and any caveats

_meta.zoneSchemaNote: When `zone` is set, the calibration script uses the species' zone-specific rarity (animal.zones[zone]) instead of the park-level rarity. Zone IDs match src/data/parkZones.js.

anchors.source: NPS Yellowstone Bison Management Plan and operational sighting logs; consistent across decades of Lamar/Hayden Valley road counts.
anchors.rationale: Bison are seen on ~100% of summer visits to Lamar/Hayden valleys — the most reliable megafauna encounter in any US park.

anchors.source: Yellowstone Wildlife Watcher Program logs; Mammoth/Madison/Lamar daily reports.
anchors.rationale: Elk are highly visible at Mammoth Hot Springs and along the Madison River; nearly every summer visitor sees them.

anchors.source: Yellowstone Wolf Project annual reports (Smith et al., 2018-2024); Lamar Valley dawn-watching success rates.
anchors.rationale: For an experienced wolf-watcher with a spotting scope at Lamar Valley dawn, sighting probability is well-documented around 30-40%. For a casual midday visitor it's <2%.

anchors.source: Yellowstone Wolf Project; Borg et al. 2016 (10.1111/1365-2664.12502) on visitor-encounter rates.
anchors.rationale: Casual midday visitors very rarely see wolves; the low single-digit % is consistent across multiple seasons of survey data.

anchors.source: NPS Yellowstone Bear Management Office annual sightings reports; consistent with informal visitor surveys.
anchors.rationale: Grizzly sightings are documented on ~15-20% of multi-day summer visits, driven by Hayden/Lamar Valley and Antelope Flats activity.

anchors.source: Crabtree & Sheldon Yellowstone coyote ecology studies; consistent with Lamar Valley operational logs.
anchors.rationale: Coyotes are highly visible year-round in open valleys; ~45% of typical-length casual visits see at least one.

anchors.source: NPS Denali Wildlife Sightings on Park Road program; published bus-tour summary stats (~70-80% caribou sighting rate June-Aug).
anchors.rationale: Park Road bus surveys explicitly publish per-tour sighting %s — the gold-standard ground-truth dataset for any US park.

anchors.source: Denali Park Road bus-tour sighting logs (NPS published).
anchors.rationale: Dall Sheep visible on the Polychrome Pass cliffs from the bus on ~85% of summer trips.

anchors.source: Denali Park Road bus tour reports; NPS visitor wildlife sightings data.
anchors.rationale: Grizzlies are sighted on ~75-85% of full Park Road bus tours during summer.

anchors.source: Denali Park Road bus-tour sighting logs.
anchors.rationale: Moose sightings happen on ~30-40% of summer bus trips — much lower than caribou/sheep due to forested habitat.

anchors.source: Denali Park Road wolf sighting program; Borg et al. 2016 noted wolf-harvest impact reduced rates from ~45% to ~5-20%.
anchors.rationale: Post-harvest sighting rates have settled around ~15-25% — much lower than pre-2010 levels but still meaningful.

anchors.source: Brooks Camp / Brooks Falls operational sighting data (NPS); webcam-confirmed daily.
anchors.rationale: Bears at Brooks Falls in July are effectively guaranteed — many tens visible from the platform on any given day.

anchors.source: Anhinga Trail / Shark Valley operational sighting logs; consistent across all seasons.
anchors.rationale: Alligators are visible from the Anhinga Trail boardwalk on essentially every visit in any season.

anchors.source: Anhinga Trail name origin; eBird Status & Trends matches.
anchors.rationale: The trail is named for them — they perch in the open along the boardwalk on essentially every visit.

anchors.source: USFWS Florida Panther Recovery Program annual reports; <230 wild panthers total.
anchors.rationale: With ~200-230 individuals total in the species' range, casual visitor encounters are vanishingly rare.

anchors.source: FWC manatee aerial survey data — park-wide average, not Flamingo-specific.
anchors.rationale: Park-wide winter manatee sighting rate is ~15% for visitors not specifically heading to Flamingo. Flamingo zone anchor (separate) tests the warm-water-refugia hotspot at 55%.

anchors.source: NPS Shenandoah Skyline Drive visitor wildlife logs.
anchors.rationale: Deer browse the meadows along Skyline Drive at all times of day — essentially every visitor sees them.

anchors.source: Shenandoah NPS Bear Sighting Reports (informal but consistent).
anchors.rationale: Bear sightings are documented on roughly a quarter of summer visits, mostly along Skyline Drive overlooks at dawn/dusk.

anchors.source: NPS Smokies park-wide elk distribution.
anchors.rationale: Park-wide fall elk sighting rate (visitors who DON'T head to Cataloochee) is ~20%. Cataloochee zone anchor (separate) tests the herd's actual location at 95%.

anchors.source: NPS Smokies Bear Management; Cades Cove sighting frequency is well-documented.

anchors.source: Cades Cove Loop deer counts.

anchors.source: RMNP elk-rut visitor management documentation; Estes Park / Moraine Park / Horseshoe Park.
